result.title: REDaCT: Collapse-Free Unlearning in Large Reasoning Models
result.comment: Accepted to Findings of EMNLP 2026. 19 pages, 7 figures, 6 tables. Copyright 2026 Association for Computational Linguistics (ACL). Licensed under CC BY 4.0
result.summary: Unlearning in large reasoning models (LRMs) requires removing forget-set information from both the reasoning trace and the final answer. Existing approaches achieve this objective at the cost of reasoning collapse, where the model fails to produce a coherent chain-of-thought (CoT) and does not properly terminate its reasoning process. To address this challenge, we propose REDaCT (REgenerate via Detection and Corrective Tuning), an inference-time unlearning framework for LRMs. REDaCT consists of two key components: (1) a binary leak detector that identifies sentences in the reasoning trace that leak forget-set information, and (2) an embedding optimization module that learns a corrective embedding offline, such that when injected at the first detected leak during inference, it guides subsequent reasoning towards sentences that do not leak forget-set information. Experimental results show that REDaCT completely avoids reasoning collapse, substantially improving reasoning preservation compared to state-of-the-art unlearning methods while maintaining perfect answer forgetting and near-perfect CoT forgetting. Our code is available at: https://github.com/jmaccoby/redact.

AI.brief_summary: 提出 REDaCT，一个面向大型推理模型的推理期遗忘框架：用二分类泄露检测器定位推理链中泄露遗忘集信息的句子，并在检测到首个泄露处注入离线学得的纠正 embedding，引导其后续推理转向不泄露的内容，从而避免推理崩溃。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「在推理中途注入纠正 embedding 以改变后续推理状态」的做法，可能为 LVR 中如何干预、更新 latent 推理状态与终止行为提供线索，可供核查该嵌入对内部表示及任务必要信息保留的影响。
